Which haue the key of Hel to open & bring forth al the old condemned here{{ls}}ies buried before in the depth.}} a {{ls}}tarre to haue fallen from heauen vpon the earth, and there vvas giuen to him the key of the pitte of bottomles depth. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=2|align=float}}† And he opened the pitte of the bottomles depth: and the {{ls}}moke of the pitte a{{ls}}cended, as the {{ls}}moke of a great fornace: and the {{ls}}unne vvas darkened & the aier vvith the {{ls}}moke of the pitte. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=3|align=float}}† And from the {{ls}}moke of the pitte there i{{ls}}{{ls}}ued forth c ∷ {{outside R|∷ c Innumerable pety heretikes folowing their Mai{{ls}}ters after the opening & the {{ls}}moke of the bottomle{{ls}}{{ls}}e pit.}} locu{{ls}}tes into the earth. and povver vvas giuen to them, as the {{ls}}corpions of the earth haue povver: {{verse|chapter=9|verse=4|align=float}}† and it vvas commaunded them that they {{ls}}hould not hurt the gra{{ls}}{{ls}}e of the earth {{sup|‖}} nor any greene thing, nor any tree: but onely men vvhich haue not the {{ls}}igne of God in their foreheads. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=5|align=float}}† and it vvas giuen vnto them that they {{ls}}hould not kil them: but that they {{ls}}hould be tormented fiue monethes: and their tormentes as the tormentes of a {{ls}}corpion vvhen he {{ls}}triketh a man. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6|align=float}}† And * {{outside L|''Apoc. 6, 16.''}} in tho{{ls}}e daies men {{ls}}hal {{ls}}eeke for death, and {{ls}}hal not finde it: and they {{ls}}hal de{{ls}}ire to die, & death {{ls}}hal flee from them.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=7|align=float}}† And the {{ls}}imilitudes of the locu{{ls}}tes, like to hor{{ls}}es {{sup|‖}} prepared into battel: and vpō their heades as it vvere crovvnes like to gold: & their faces as the faces of men. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=8|align=float}}† And they had heare as the heare of vvomen: & their teeth vvere as of lions. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=9|align=float}}† And they had ∷ {{outside R|∷ ''c coats of mail, or other coats of fence.''}} habbergions as habbergions of yron, and the voice of their vvinges as the voice of the chariotes of many hor{{ls}}es running into battel. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=10|align=float}}† and they had tailes like to {{ls}}corpions, and {{ls}}tinges vvere in their tailes: and their povver vvas to hurt men fiue monethes. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11|align=float}}† ∷ {{outside R|∷ The cheefe Mai{{ls}}ter of heretikes.}} and they had ouer them a king, the Angel of the bottomles depth, vvho{{ls}}e name in Hebrevv is ''Abaddon'', and in Greeke ''Apollyon'': in Latin hauing the name ''Exterminans''. ∷ {{outside R|∷ ''אבדון {{lang|grc|ἀπολλύων}},'' In Engli{{ls}}h, ''De{{ls}}troier.''}} {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12|align=float}}† One vvoe is gone, & behold two vvoes come yet after the{{ls}}e.
